newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland Cotton sees steady result.
newsitem.headline: Queensland Cotton sees steady result.

text.p: Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to post a similar result in the year to end-February 1998 to that achieved in 1996/97.
"We continue to expect that our February 1998 results for the Australian operations can duplicate the outstanding February 1997 outcome," chairman Ben Macdonald told the annual meeting.
In the year to February 28, 1997 Queensland Cotton posted a net profit of A$13.26 million compared with A$8.03 million the previous year.
Macdonald said forecasts for the 1996/97 Australian cotton crop were firming up, with the latest estimates standing at 2.75 million bales.
"We have already advised of an expectation that ginning volumes this year will be down marginally on the previous year's record," Macdonald said.
However, Queensland Cotton was looking to gain in merchandising and marketing to compensate for this reduction, he said.

Macdonald told shareholders that despite fears of another drought-bringing El Nino weather pattern all indications were that the 1997/98 cotton crop would be a record, exceeding the peak 1996/97 estimate.

"Although planting will not occur until at least October 1997, good water supplies, strong prices and favourable conditions generally point towards a cotton crop which pushes us towards the three million bale mark," he said.
The industry group Cotton Australia has forecast that Australia will process a record 2.7 million bales of cotton in 1996/97, equivalent to 612,000 tonnes of cotton.
The company earlier announced it had agreed to buy the U.S. Anderson Clayton Corp cotton business of the Swiss-based Volkart Group for about US$43 million.
Macdonald said the acquisition would make Queensland Cotton the largest ginning company in the world.
Queensland Cotton shares were steady at A$5.50 at 11.15 a.m. (0130 GMT).
